_note: Paraphrased distillations of ideas from sources in research/REPORT.md (ids B*, L*, S*). Not quotations.

principles.title: Meaning is found in adopting responsibility
principles.summary: Meaning scales with responsibility voluntarily taken on; people without a 'load' tend to drift, get anxious and depressed.

principles.title: Aim structures perception
principles.summary: Without a hierarchy of values you cannot decide what to look at or do; if everything is equally important you are paralysed.

principles.title: Order and chaos
principles.summary: Order: actions produce expected results. Chaos: the map stops matching the world. Grow by confronting the unknown in manageable doses.

principles.title: Compare yourself to who you were yesterday, not to who someone else is today
principles.summary: Measure progress against your past self; set small incremental goals that are slightly better than yesterday and let them compound. Verified against B1 Rule 4 summaries and L13.

principles.title: Small, slightly-better steps compound
principles.summary: Aim high but make the goal difficult but proximal; ask what small thing you could do, that you would actually do, to make things an increment better, reward yourself for incremental movement, and raise the baseline over time - incremental improvement repeated is virtually unstoppable. Verified: B1 Rule 4 passage and JBP's own words (L13, L15).

principles.title: Treat yourself like someone you are responsible for helping
principles.summary: Care for your own well-being as you would for someone in your charge.

principles.title: Pursue what is meaningful, not what is expedient
principles.summary: Expedience trades the future for the present.

principles.title: Set your house in perfect order before you criticize the world
principles.summary: Fix what is within reach before blaming the world.

principles.title: Tell the truth, or at least don't lie
principles.summary: Truthful speech keeps your map accurate and relationships trustworthy; self-deception corrupts both.

principles.title: Assume the person you are listening to might know something you don't
principles.summary: Summarize the other person's view to their satisfaction before replying.

principles.title: Be precise in your speech
principles.summary: Naming a problem precisely makes it smaller and solvable.

principles.title: Do not hide unwanted things in the fog
principles.summary: Avoided problems compound into larger ones.

principles.title: Imagine who you could be and then aim single-mindedly at that
principles.summary: A vivid desirable future and a feared one give direction.

principles.title: Notice that opportunity lurks where responsibility has been abdicated
principles.summary: Problems nobody handles are openings.

principles.title: Do not do what you hate
principles.summary: Repeatedly acting against conscience erodes you.

principles.title: Work as hard as you possibly can on at least one thing and see what happens
principles.summary: Concentrated effort reveals capability.

principles.title: If old memories still upset you, write them down carefully and completely
principles.summary: Memories still emotionally hot after ~18 months signal an unextracted lesson.

principles.title: Plan and work diligently to maintain the romance in your relationship
principles.summary: Romance is a practiced skill; partners must say clearly what they want and negotiate.

principles.title: Do not allow yourself to become resentful, deceitful, or arrogant
principles.summary: Resentment signals either immaturity or a need to speak up.

principles.title: Be grateful in spite of your suffering
principles.summary: Gratitude and love are deliberate practices.

principles.title: Harmless is not virtuous
principles.summary: Someone capable of standing up for themselves who chooses restraint is virtuous; over-agreeable people get exploited and resentful.

principles.title: Even if it's only 5% me, fix it
principles.summary: In recurring conflict fix your share; aim to solve, not win.

principles.title: Suffering is real; reducing it is meaningful
principles.summary: People act as if pain is real; reducing needless suffering gives meaning.

principles.title: Abandon ideology
principles.summary: Totalizing one-cause explanations replace personal responsibility.

principles.title: Learn to negotiate on your own behalf
principles.summary: Agreeable people bargain harder for others than for themselves and are prone to being exploited. The remedy is not hostility but saying what you think and negotiating for yourself, with a real alternative in hand, while keeping the balance (not too disagreeable).

principles.title: Sacrifice the present for a better future
principles.summary: Making today a little less impulsively pleasurable to make tomorrow more secure is the core of maturity and the archaic meaning of sacrifice.

principles.title: Confront what threatens you, voluntarily
principles.summary: When chaotic, threatening things upset you, open your eyes and face them; avoided chaos grows.
